Hello! Any other archaeology students or professionals active in this subverse?
Yup, me. I'm working on remote sensing in archaeology right now.
Could you expand a little on that, please? :)

Yeah, what I'm doing is I'm building my own systems to try to get complete data control on a site. That means being able to record the entire site in full as stages of the excavation are completed. Coastal sites and shipwrecks are what I'm working toward eventually so I can marry SONAR imaging with everything else, but what I'm doing now is using UAVs to capture extremely high resolution, geometrically corrected, georeferenced orthophotography and create an accurate digital elevation model (DEM) of a site before it's even touched, then using a multicopter to take more high resolution images of the actual excavation spots as each one gets done. So when I have everything (like 12GB worth of shit for even a tiny site) loaded up in a GIS or something, you can peel down through the layers and visualize the site however you want. On top of that, with a sub-meter GPS you can take highly accurate points and assign whatever was found at that point as an attribute in ArcMap.

So basically, with my data system, you can start at the untouched site, peel down to the excavated features, and then open up points associated with the test units or shovel tests that list what is associated with that unit. On top of that, the othrophotography is good enough that you can actually digitze the whole damn site right from the aerial images and create your vector maps and everything else without having to do it the old fashioned way.
